R03.text: In the recent 14 days, your resting heart rate rose notably from a baseline average of ~51.8 bpm to ~61.7 bpm, persisting throughout the window. Sleep duration (~472 min), steps (~7,923), active minutes (~56), low movement, and HRV RMSSD (~45 ms) all stayed near your 28-day baselines. Your sleep timing and 07:00 wake time were unchanged. The sustained RHR shift occurred without corresponding changes in other tracked metrics. Consider whether device fit or recording conditions changed.

R04.text: During your 28-day baseline, your sleep was consistent (~471 min, ~22:50–07:00), steps averaged ~7,938/day, active minutes ~55/day, and resting heart rate ~52 bpm. Over the recent 14 days, sleep timing, duration, steps (~7,923), active minutes (~56), low-movement minutes, and HRV (~45 ms) all remained close to baseline. The notable change is your resting heart rate, which rose to ~62 bpm—about 10 bpm above your baseline range of 51–53. This elevation was persistent across all 14 window days. While device estimates can vary, a sustained shift of this size relative to your own baseline is worth noting for continued monitoring.

R05.text: Over 28 baseline days with complete wear, metrics were stable: sleep ~471 min ending exactly at 07:00 daily, steps ~7938, activity ~55 min, low movement ~450 min, resting HR ~51.8 bpm, and RMSSD ~44.8 ms. In the 14-day window, resting HR rose abruptly to ~61.7 bpm (+10 bpm, +19%) from day one and persisted throughout. All other metrics remained near baseline levels: sleep ~472 min, steps ~7923, activity ~56 min, low movement ~447 min, and RMSSD ~45.1 ms. Sleep timing, weekday/weekend structure, and paired correlations were unchanged. The HR shift was sustained without return toward baseline.

R06.text: Across 28 baseline days, sleep averaged 471 min (start ~22:49, end 07:00), steps ~7938/day, activity ~55 min, RHR ~52 bpm, RMSSD ~45 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep timing, duration (~472 min), steps (~7923), activity (~56 min), low movement (~447), and RMSSD (~45) all remained stable relative to baseline. Resting heart rate increased abruptly by ~10 bpm to ~62, persisting throughout the window (range 61-63) without return toward baseline. Weekday/weekend structure was consistent. Paired correlations between metrics were weak or absent in both periods.

R07.text: During your recent 14-day window, most patterns matched your 28-day baseline: sleep averaged ~472 min (baseline ~471) ending consistently at 07:00, steps ~7,923 vs ~7,938, activity ~56 vs ~55 min, and RMSSD ~45 ms throughout. One notable change is resting heart rate, which rose from a very steady ~52 bpm baseline to ~62 bpm across all 14 window days—a persistent ~10 bpm increase without corresponding changes in sleep, activity, or HRV. This sustained shift may warrant checking whether the device fit or measurement conditions changed.

R09.text: During the 28-day baseline, sleep averaged 471 min (start ~22:50, end fixed 07:00), steps ~7938, activity ~55 min, RHR ~52 bpm, RMSSD ~45 ms. In the 14-day window, RHR rose abruptly by ~10 bpm to ~62 and persisted throughout, while sleep, steps, activity, low movement, and RMSSD remained near baseline levels. audit.audit_limitations: This audit is a provisional LLM analysis based solely on the supplied synthetic wearable JSON and knowledge snippets. It cannot establish clinical truth, diagnose any condition, or determine the cause of the observed resting heart rate change. The PROVISIONAL_LLM_GOLD labels are fallible relevance indicators, not human ground truth. No external data sources were consulted, and no tool calls were made. Representations were evaluated only against the provided raw observations and arithmetic seeds; subtle numerical discrepancies in rounding or qualitative phrasing were assessed for material accuracy rather than exact string matching. The absence of posture, substance, medication, or device-fit data limits interpretation of metric changes.
